cards.text: Ezra the priest is facedown before the house of God, praying to his God. Israelites, even priests and Levites, have married women from the peoples around them, and Ezra is weeping as he confesses that unfaithfulness (Ezra 9:1-2). And while he's down there, he's not alone for long.

cards.question: While Ezra prays facedown before the house of God, who gathers around him?

answers.text: A very large assembly of Israelites

cards.question: The crowd around Ezra is men, women and children, and they weep bitterly too.

cards.text: Then Shecaniah son of Jehiel, an Elamite, speaks up to Ezra: we have been unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women from the people of the land. Notice he says WE, friend, not 'some guys I know from work.'

cards.question: Shecaniah admits Israel has been unfaithful, yet he says there is still ___ for Israel.

cards.text: And Shecaniah's got a plan. He wants it done according to the Law, following the counsel of those who tremble at the command of God.

cards.question: What covenant does Shecaniah want the people to make before God?

answers.text: Send away the foreign wives and their children
Rebuild the walls all around Jerusalem
Keep a fast for forty days and nights

cards.text: Then Shecaniah turns to Ezra: "Get up, for this matter is your responsibility" and he doesn't stop there.

cards.question: When Shecaniah tells Ezra to get up and take action, what does he promise him?

answers.text: The people will pick a new leader
The people will return to Babylon

cards.text: So Ezra gets up. I know that move, friend. I spent YEARS flat on my back in a junk drawer, and getting up is the hardest part.

cards.question: Ezra makes the leading priests, Levites and all Israel ___ to do what Shecaniah said.
The priests, Levites and all Israel refuse to take Ezra's oath.

cards.text: Then Ezra leaves the front of the house of God and walks to the chamber of a man named Jehohanan son of Eliashib. He's mourning over the unfaithfulness of the exiles.

cards.question: While Ezra stays in Jehohanan's chamber, he eats no food and drinks no water.

cards.text: Then a proclamation goes out across Judah and Jerusalem. Every exile, gather at Jerusalem.

cards.question: The exiles get ___ days to show up in Jerusalem.
What happens to any exile who doesn't show up in Jerusalem in time?

answers.text: He loses his property and is expelled from the assembly
He pays a fine in silver to the house of God
He is sent back to Babylon to live for good

cards.text: THREE DAYS. Not 'whenever you get a chance,' not 'let's circle back next week.' And within three days, all the men of Judah and Benjamin show up in Jerusalem.

cards.question: On the twentieth day of the ninth month, everyone sits in the square at the house of God, trembling over this matter. What else has them trembling?

cards.text: Then Ezra the priest stands up in front of all of them and says it plainly: "You have been unfaithful by marrying foreign women, adding to the guilt of Israel."

cards.question: Ezra tells them to make a confession to the LORD, do His will, and ___ themselves from the people of the land and from their foreign wives.
The whole assembly argues with Ezra and refuses to do what he says.

cards.text: They shout back, "Truly we must do as you say!" Then comes the BUT: there are a lot of people, it's the rainy season, they can't stay out in the open, and this isn't the work of one or two days.

cards.question: With so many people and the rain coming down, how does the assembly suggest dealing with the men who married foreign women?

answers.text: Leaders represent everyone while towns come at set times
Each family handles its own case quietly at home
Everyone gathers again once the rainy season ends

cards.question: In the assembly's plan, each town's men who married foreign women come at an appointed time with the ___ and ___ of their town.
Every single person in the assembly agrees with this plan.

cards.text: Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah oppose the plan, with Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite supporting them.
But the exiles go ahead and do as proposed. Ezra the priest picks men to represent their families, every one of them identified by name.

cards.question: What kind of men does Ezra pick to represent their families?

cards.text: On the first day of the tenth month, they launch the investigation. Remember when the crowd said this wasn't the work of one or two days? They were NOT exaggerating.

cards.question: By the first day of the first month, they've dealt with all the men who married foreign women.

cards.text: Then comes the list, family by family, of every man who had married a foreign woman. It starts with priests from the family of Jeshua son of Jozadak, who pledged to send their wives away and gave a ram as a guilt offering. Then come Levites, a singer, gatekeepers and men from across Israel, and some of them had children by these wives.

findings.problem: The joke adds to Papa Dorin's backstory. It says he spent years 'flat on my back' in the drawer and that 'getting up is the hardest part,' which implies he got himself up. In his backstory he never gets himself out. He is called out of the drawer by the angel and renewed by the Most High. The comparison also doesn't line up: Ezra is facedown in prayer and confession, and Papa Dorin was lying discarded, so the shared action of getting up doesn't click cleanly.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: Stop 2's story cards are stripped down to plain narration with almost none of Papa Dorin's voice. Cards 1, 4, 8, 9 and 13 read like a summary, and the only light line in the whole stop is card 11's 'They were NOT exaggerating.' Moments like the crowd's 'Truly we must do as you say!' followed by the BUT, the rainy-season logistics, and the handful of men who oppose the plan could each carry a real Papa Dorin reaction without muddying a fact.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The walkthrough never tells the reason the assembly gives for its plan in Ezra 10:14: it is to continue 'until the fierce anger of our God in this matter is turned away from us.' Card 4 also drops 'for we have transgressed greatly in this matter' (10:13). The fierce anger of God is the stated purpose of the whole process, so the baker leaves without an important detail of the passage.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
